name: The Hausa kings of Zazzau go into exile

summary.text: When the jihad took Zaria in December 1808, Sarkin Zazzau Muhammadu Makau led much of the Hausa nobility south to Zuba, one of four Koro chiefdoms that paid Zazzau tribute. In 1828 his brother and successor Abu Ja (Jatau) founded a new town, Abuja, walled it the next year, and reigned there as Sarkin Zazzau. Fulani Zaria attacked it repeatedly and failed; the kingdom stayed free until the British occupied it in 1902.

routes.label: From Zaria to Zuba, then Abuja

moments.title: Zaria falls
moments.text: Malam Musa takes Zaria for the jihad.

moments.title: Refuge at Zuba
moments.text: Makau settles among the Koro at Zuba.

moments.title: Abuja founded
moments.text: Abu Ja founds Abuja, today's Suleja, and walls it in 1829.
